items.title: FAA ground stop disruptions extend into Monday
items.feedTitle: Flight disruptions expected to last into Monday
items.summary: A nationwide aviation ground stop that occurred Friday has caused continued flight disruptions into the following week. Congress allocated $12.5 billion to upgrade the aging air traffic control system, though President Trump is requesting additional funding. Transportation officials are working to restore normal operations after the unprecedented grounding.

items.title: Democrat Mary Peltola extends lead in Alaska Senate race
items.feedTitle: Peltola's lead increases in uncalled Alaska Senate race
items.summary: Democratic candidate Mary Peltola continues to grow her lead in Alaska's closely watched Senate race as vote counting proceeds. Multiple outlets report her position strengthening, though the race remains officially uncalled. The outcome could have implications for the balance of power in Congress.

items.title: Steering failure preceded New Orleans tanker-cruise ship collision
items.feedTitle: Preliminary investigation points to steering failure in tanker collision with river cruise ship
items.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board released preliminary findings that the Atlantic Asphalt tanker suffered a steering casualty approximately two minutes before colliding with the American Heritage cruise ship on the Mississippi River. The incident, dubbed the 'miracle on the Mississippi,' resulted in no fatalities despite over 130 people being rescued. The port of New Orleans has sued the tanker's owners for at least $1 million in damages.

items.title: Massive waves pummel California coast, close beaches
items.feedTitle: Huge waves pummel California coast, forcing closure of popular piers
items.summary: Huge waves up to 50 feet high battered the Southern California coast, forcing the closure of popular piers in Ventura, Hermosa Beach, and Manhattan Beach. The National Weather Service issued warnings as storms brought dangerous surf conditions and coastal flooding. Additional storms were expected to continue impacting the region through the weekend.

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak remains out of control after six months
items.feedTitle: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo 6 months into response
items.summary: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded more than 11,000 cases with nearly half of those infected dying, according to government data. At six months into the response, the outbreak remains uncontrolled and is on track to surpass the death toll from the 2014-2016 West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people. The crisis underscores ongoing challenges in containing the disease.

stlouis.title: Missouri Senator Schmitt pushes $30B aviation modernization bill
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri Sen. Eric Schmitt pushes $30 billion aviation modernization bill after FAA ground stop
stlouis.summary: Sen. Eric Schmitt is advocating for a $30 billion aviation modernization initiative in response to Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop. The proposal aims to modernize the nation's aging air traffic control infrastructure. Schmitt's push comes as Congress debates funding for aviation system upgrades.

stlouis.title: Cardinals prospect faces uncertain future with St. Louis
stlouis.feedTitle: Cardinals Former Top Prospect's Days In St. Louis May Be Numbered
stlouis.summary: A former top prospect in the St. Louis Cardinals organization may be on his way out of the organization, according to recent reporting. The prospect's status with the team remains unclear as the organization evaluates its roster.

stlouis.title: St. Louis Blues goalie becomes trade market focus
stlouis.feedTitle: NHL Rumours: Trade Market on St. Louis Blues Goalie
stlouis.summary: The goaltender for the NHL's St. Louis Blues has become a subject of trade speculation as teams assess potential roster upgrades. Multiple reports suggest interest from other franchises in acquiring the netminder.

items.title: Iran launches drone attacks on US military base in Bahrain
items.feedTitle: Iran launches drone attacks against US military base in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran carried out a six-drone attack on a U.S. military base in Bahrain early Sunday, with Bahrain claiming it intercepted the strikes before they hit their targets. Iran claimed it struck the base, marking a resumption of escalatory actions in the region. The attack raises concerns about potential escalation in ongoing tensions between Tehran and Washington.

items.title: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rally against media restrictions
items.feedTitle: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs protest in Prague over media freedom
items.summary: An estimated 350,000 Czechs gathered in Prague to protest the government's plan to shift public media funding from mandatory licence fees to the state budget. Protesters argued the change would undermine media independence and freedom. The Czech government insists broadcasters need to cut costs, but opponents fear government control over content.

items.title: Pope condemns murders of Peru's Indigenous environmental leaders
items.feedTitle: Pope condemns murders of Peru’s Indigenous leaders, deforestation of Amazon
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV demanded justice for Indigenous environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon during his visit to Peru. The pontiff spoke forcefully on the final day of his Latin America tour, backing Indigenous efforts to stop deforestation and illegal mining that threaten the rainforest and local communities. His remarks highlighted the violence faced by those defending the Amazon.

items.title: Australian MP discharged from hospital after leg amputation
items.feedTitle: Australian MP who lost both legs in alleged car attack discharged from hospital
items.summary: Independent Australian MP Helen Haines was discharged from hospital four weeks after being allegedly attacked by a man outside her electorate office in regional Victoria, during which she lost both of her legs. The attack occurred over a month ago, and her discharge marks a significant milestone in her recovery process. The incident remains under investigation.

items.title: Bangladeshi garment workers strike over wage demands
items.feedTitle: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
items.summary: Clothing factories in Bangladesh have shut down as workers strike demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (approximately £182) per month. The strike highlights ongoing tensions between workers seeking better pay and conditions and manufacturers resisting wage increases. The labor action reflects broader concerns about worker compensation in Bangladesh's garment industry.

items.title: AIIMS Delhi performs India's first open fetal surgery
items.feedTitle: AIIMS Delhi performs India’s first open fetal surgery to repair severe spinal defect
items.summary: AIIMS Delhi has performed India's first open fetal surgery to repair a severe spinal defect at 25 weeks of gestation, a medical milestone for the country. The procedure represents a significant advancement in fetal surgical capabilities and prenatal care in India. The successful operation demonstrates the hospital's expertise in complex fetal interventions.

items.title: Search operation launched after Kulgam CRPF post attack
items.feedTitle: Kulgam terror attack: Search operation launched in J&K to hunt terrorists who attacked CRPF post
items.summary: A major search operation has been launched in Jammu and Kashmir following an attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam. Hundreds of people have been questioned and detained as counter-insurgency operations intensify. The incident revives concerns about militant activity in the Kashmir region.

items.feedTitle: Chinese Military Aircraft Reportedly Enters Indian Airspace Over Sikkim
items.summary: A Chinese military aircraft allegedly breached Indian airspace over Sikkim, hovering for approximately 20 minutes according to reports. Indian officials and the IAF have not yet confirmed the incident. The alleged incursion raises tensions along the India-China border.

items.title: India lifted 500 million people from poverty but survival remains precarious
items.feedTitle: India pulled 500m people out of poverty. Many of them still barely survive
items.summary: Despite India pulling 500 million people out of poverty over recent decades, many remain in precarious economic situations with minimal resources to sustain themselves. The World Bank report highlights that while poverty reduction has been significant, the sustainability and quality of life improvements remain concerning for newly emerged populations. The findings underscore ongoing development challenges.

immigration.title: US revokes over 6,000 visas in birth tourism crackdown
immigration.feedTitle: Crackdown Against Birth Tourism: US Cancels 6000 Visas
immigration.summary: The United States has revoked over 6,000 visas as part of an expanded crackdown on birth tourism and related immigration fraud. The State Department implemented the policy to prevent foreign nationals from using US citizenship as a mechanism for anchor family visas. The revocation represents one of the largest visa cancellations in recent history and is now in effect.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending deference on H-1B visa extensions
immigration.feedTitle: DHS wants every H-1B extension reviewed from scratch; the rule is only proposed and comments close November 13
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed ending the USCIS deference rule, which requires each H-1B extension to be reviewed from scratch rather than automatically approved if the initial petition was approved. The proposal, still pending and not yet finalized, could impact approximately 208,000 work visa renewals and trigger additional requests for evidence. Comments on the proposed rule closed November 13, and the final rule has not yet been issued.

immigration.title: IBM ends H-1B sponsorship for most consulting roles
immigration.feedTitle: IBM to end H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles amid Trump's immigration crackdown — Report
immigration.summary: IBM has announced it will end H-1B visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting division by the end of 2026. The move comes amid the Trump administration's broader immigration crackdown targeting skilled visa workers. The decision reflects broader industry concerns about the uncertain future of the H-1B program.

cards.title: Batch similar tasks to minimize context switching
cards.insight: Our brains perform best when holding one complex idea. Switching between email, reports, and meetings fragments attention and increases the time needed to re-engage with deep work.
cards.takeaway: Block 90 minutes for one task type daily—write all emails in one batch, hold all meetings in one window, do all analysis together.

cards.title: Use friction as a focus tool, not a barrier
cards.insight: Low friction enables distraction (notifications always on, apps always open). Strategic friction—closing unnecessary tabs, phone in another room, silencing notifications—redirects mental energy back to intention.
cards.takeaway: Add one deliberate friction point: turn off notifications for 2 hours, close Slack, or move your phone. Notice how focus sharpens.

cards.title: Endings boost focus more than beginnings
cards.insight: We focus better with a deadline than a to-do. A time-boxed end creates urgency and commitment; an open-ended task invites procrastination and drift.
cards.takeaway: For each focus block, set a visible timer and a specific end state ('report draft done by 2 pm') rather than vague goals.

cards.title: Recovery time is part of focus, not a break from it
cards.insight: A 5-minute walk or window stare after deep work isn't wasted time—it consolidates learning, prevents burnout, and readies the brain for the next challenge. Grinding continuously depletes focus reserves.
cards.takeaway: After each 90-minute focus block, take a 10-minute genuine break—no email, no scrolling—before the next task.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO arrives as AI sector seeks confidence amid turmoil
ai.feedTitle: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
ai.summary: Anthropic is set for a November 19 Nasdaq IPO with $900 billion in commitments, positioning itself as a major test of investor confidence in the AI sector following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. The company has emerged as a leading alternative to OpenAI and Google in large language model development. The IPO timing is critical as the broader AI industry confronts questions about leadership, governance, and competitive dynamics.

ai.title: Congress tightens export rules on AI chips after Nvidia scandal
ai.feedTitle: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
ai.summary: Congress is moving to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips in response to the Nvidia scandal involving alleged illegal sales to China through intermediaries. The legislative action aims to prevent repeat scenarios where banned chips reach Chinese AI developers. The crackdown reflects national security concerns about maintaining US dominance in AI infrastructure.

ai.title: South Korean tax exam top scorer admits to AI cheating
ai.feedTitle: Mini camera, AI and smartphone: How tax exam top scorer says he cheated under two proctors’ noses
ai.summary: Han Won-seok, the top scorer on South Korea's national tax accountancy exam with a near-perfect mark, has confessed to using a hidden camera and AI to cheat the test. He sent photos of exam questions to an AI tool for assistance, undermining the integrity of the high-stakes assessment. The admission raises concerns about cheating in national college entrance exams scheduled the following week.

ai.title: Jensen Huang was having multiple affairs, Reuters reports
ai.feedTitle: Jensen Huang was having a third affair, Reuters reports
ai.summary: Reuters reported that Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang was involved in a third affair with another Nvidia employee, in addition to the alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy that led to his resignation. The expanded revelations add to questions about corporate governance and Huang's judgment during his tenure leading the company. The company has not confirmed details of all alleged relationships.

ai.title: Indian startup Bharat Semi secures $24M seed funding for AI sensors
ai.feedTitle: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
ai.summary: Bharat Semi, an Indian chip startup, has raised $24 million in seed funding to develop AI-enabled sensor technology for the global market. The company has already secured design wins with major customers including General Atomics. The funding reflects growing interest in Indian AI chip startups competing in the broader semiconductor landscape.
